Marta: Heads-up: Product wants to dark-launch residency routing today. Need a quick ops + security sanity check. Goal: active/active but honor tenant residency without SDK changes.
Aj: Proposal: use an edge-only verified header X-RW-Residency: eu|na|none. SDKs may include it but edge verifies against control-plane signed policy.
sre-simon: That seems ok. We need metrics for: misroute_count, residency_enforced_count, and residency_failures. Also, avoid cache stampedes when routing changes.
Chen: Two hard things: header spoofing and KV locality. Edge must only accept header when control-plane policy authorizes tenant. For KV: either replicate tiny prefix stores to EU or introduce async priming.
Marta: Agreed. Operational model: edge fetches signed residency assertion (short TTL) from control-plane. If assertion says "eu,enforce": true -> edge routes to EU cluster. Edge includes X-Res-Verified: sig-id header when forwarding.
Aj: Flow sketch:
```
client -> edge (get residency assertion from control-plane cache)
edge -> dataplane: X-RW-Residency: eu; X-Res-Verified: <sig-id>
```
Edge routing respects assertion + capacity signals.
sre-simon: For caching we should do lightweight prefix replication for residency tenants only. Full KV geo-replication is too costly. Idea: replicate hot prefixes and rely on cross-region read-forwarding for cold keys. Track residency_cache_local_miss metric.
Chen: Can we gate the feature? During canary, only honor assertions for tenants in list. Also reject any assertion older than TTL.
Marta: Legal asked for audit logs retention. legal-elaine: We need auditable residency_decision logs (tenant, timestamp, edge-id, decision, fallback) retained 90 days. Must be immutable.
ops-ryan: Deploy-bot: dark-launch canary started: res-routing-v1 -> 3% traffic. Canary id canary-486. Monitor error delta and tail latency. Pause threshold: +0.5% error rate or +60ms p95.
Aj: Control-plane assertion sample (read-only):
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-123",
  "residency": "eu",
  "enforce": true,
  "expires_at": "2026-04-15T12:00:00Z",
  "sig": "base64sig"
}
```
Edge caches assertion keyed by tenant.
Chen: Fallback policies? If EU capacity is exhausted: options = strict(reject 409), queue_for_eu, degrade(route to nearest). Recommend per-tenant policy. Default: degrade for paid, strict only when legal_enforce flag true.
sre-simon: Add circuit-breaker to avoid oscillation: once a tenant is rerouted due to capacity, cooldown 30s, and emit residency_reroute_event.
Marta: Action items: Aj -> PR for header + assertion protocol + example edge pseudo-code. Chen -> cache replication playbook + simulation numbers for EU vs. NA latency. SRE-simon -> observability dashboards + canary automations. legal-elaine -> retention SLA for audit events. ops-ryan -> watch canary and be ready to rollback.
Aj: I'll drop the PR in ~1hr.
Chen: I'll run a cache-prime sim and post results tomorrow AM.
Marta: If canary looks good after 4 hours we expand to 20% then 50% over a few days. Any objections?
legal-elaine: One more  audit trail must include fallback decisions for compliance requests.
ops-ryan: Noted. Canary id canary-486 is live. Pausing criteria configured.
Marta: Thanks team. Small follow-up: include a short, operator-friendly runbook for when strict tenants hit capacity (who to call, emergency allocation steps).
Aj: Will include runbook in PR.
